sections.technique: Canine, 9 years old, Boxer breed, MR modality, brain region, analysis status: success
sections.findings: [F1] code=BRAIN-EXTRA-AXIAL-MASS | status=suspected | location=right frontal lobe, convexity | Broad-based extra-axial mass at the right frontal convexity, T1 isointense with strong homogeneous contrast enhancement and a dural tail.[S1]; [F2] code=BRAIN-PERILESIONAL-EDEMA | status=possible | location=right frontal white matter | T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the surrounding white matter consistent with vasogenic edema.[S4]; [F3] code=BRAIN-MIDLINE-SHIFT | status=uncertain | location=falx cerebri | Mild leftward deviation of the falx.[S2]; No findings returned or analysis failed for other sequences.
sections.impression: The most likely interpretation is a primary brain tumor with dural tail, supported by [F1]. Differential diagnoses include secondary brain tumors and normal anatomical variations, as suggested by [S4] and [S2].
sections.recommendations: Full manual review recommended. Additional sequences (e.g., CT, angiography) may be necessary to confirm the diagnosis. Consultation with a neurologist or veterinary oncologist is advised.

sections.findings: [F1] Lentiform hyperattenuating extra-axial collection along the left parietal convexity [S2], [F2] Linear non-displaced lucency of the left parietal bone [S2]. No findings in other regions.
sections.impression: Lentiform hyperattenuating extra-axial collection along the left parietal convexity is suspected, but its nature and cause are uncertain. Linear non-displaced lucency of the left parietal bone may be a fracture or trauma-related finding. Differential diagnoses include: [D1] Spinal meningeal tumor, [D2] Traumatic fracture, [D3] Inflammatory process.
sections.recommendations: Full manual review recommended due to uncertain findings and lack of clinical history. Additional CT sequences (e.g., sagittal, coronal) may be necessary to evaluate the extra-axial collection and left parietal bone in more detail. Consultation with a neurologist or veterinary surgeon is advised.
